manual.homelink_furnace.title: HomeLink Furnace — Manual
manual.homelink_furnace.start.title: 1 / 6 · Getting started
manual.homelink_furnace.start.body: Place the furnace facing you in clear, loaded space. Tier II occupies 2×1×1; tier III occupies 2×2×2. Connect an HE network to the copper lightning port, then add smeltable items. Open any part to view the machine. Only server SMELTING recipes are supported, including compatible datapacks. HomeLink Furnace accepts no fuel.
manual.homelink_furnace.energy.title: 2 / 6 · Energy
manual.homelink_furnace.energy.body: The furnace consumes HE exclusively through the HomeCore input port. It never produces energy or accepts FE/RF. A 200-tick recipe costs 100 HE by default. Faster tiers shorten processing without reducing energy per item. Cold warmup costs additional HE. The buffer charges while switched off; outputs remain extractible without power.
manual.homelink_furnace.ports.title: 3 / 6 · Inputs and outputs
manual.homelink_furnace.ports.body: Cyan arrow: item input. Amber arrow: item output. Copper lightning: HE input. Automation inserts only smeltable input and extracts only output. Jobs reserve their input outside automation handlers. Storage Pipes can use HomeCore ItemPort without a Furnace dependency on Storage. No items are pushed automatically. The Settings tab shows the port positions for this tier.
manual.homelink_furnace.jobs.title: 4 / 6 · Heat and jobs
manual.homelink_furnace.jobs.body: Cold machines warm before production. Hot machines start new jobs immediately, hold heat briefly when idle, then cool. Tiers have 2, 4 and 8 parallel lanes. No HE pauses progress exactly. If the output fills, finished items remain safely reserved in their lane. Free output space to resume. Jobs, stored energy and XP persist; unloaded machines do no offline catch-up.
manual.homelink_furnace.network.title: 5 / 6 · Redstone and HomeNetwork
manual.homelink_furnace.network.body: Settings offers Ignore signal, Require signal and Require no signal. Redstone conditions combine with the power switch. Switching off pauses work and cools the machine. HomeCore governs VIEW, CONTROL, CONFIGURE and MANAGE_NETWORK. Choose an authorized network and apply it; choosing Unbound detaches. Renaming uses the official HomeCore contract. Automated production credits the persistent owner when known.
Waiting for HE: check the copper port and the external power network. Output full: extract finished items. Input empty: supply a valid SMELTING recipe. Invalid recipe after reload: unfinished reserved inputs are returned safely. Unloaded multiblock parts pause checks until loaded; no chunks are forced. Completed operations store recipe XP. Collect XP requires CONTROL. Automation never collects XP. Survival dismantling releases the XP once.
viewer.homelink_furnace.intro: Industrial electric SMELTING, using HE only. No fuel, FE or RF.
viewer.homelink_furnace.tier.1: Tier I: 1×1×1, 2 lanes, speed ×1, 9 input / 9 output, 2,000 HE.
viewer.homelink_furnace.tier.2: Tier II: 2×1×1, 4 lanes, speed ×1.5, 18 input / 18 output, 6,000 HE.
viewer.homelink_furnace.tier.3: Tier III: 2×2×2, 8 lanes, speed ×2, 27 input / 27 output, 16,000 HE.
viewer.homelink_furnace.heat: Cold warmup consumes HE. A hot machine resumes immediately. Speed never reduces recipe energy cost.
viewer.homelink_furnace.xp: Recipe XP is stored and collected manually. Full output preserves finished results.
viewer.homelink_furnace.redstone: Three redstone modes, HomeCore power, naming, permissions and HomeNetwork integration.
